disposition_reason: Per-sample XRF and ICP-MS concentrations of As, Pb, Cr, Ni and other elements in 12 geophagic materials consumed in Limpopo are printed in Table 2.

study.design: field collection of geophagic materials with geochemistry, bioaccessibility (PBET) and health risk assessment
study.origin: collected from home yards, mining dumps, riverbeds and a hill at Driekop, Ga-Motodi and Taung, Fetakgomo Tubatse Local Municipality, Limpopo, South Africa
study.market: not purchased (collected where residents collect material)
study.method: Major elements by XRF on fused glass discs; trace elements (As, Cr, Co, Cu, Pb, Mn, Ni, Zn) by ICP-MS after microwave HNO3/HCl digestion

unresolved: Basis (dry or as collected) not stated for the trace-element digestion; major elements were dried at 105 °C before fusion.
No detection limits or reference material reported.
Three Driekop samples come from mining dumps, so site context mixes ordinary and mining-affected material.
Arsenic is total arsenic; cadmium and mercury were not measured.
Per-sample bioaccessibility values are figure-only (Fig. 6) and were not extracted.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Hazard index for adults ingesting the materials

regulatory_or_exposure.value: As 0.005-11.9% stomach, 1.2-12.9% intestinal; Mn up to 62.7%; Cr up to 12.9% (TAU-03); values per sample are figure-only (Fig. 6)
